'''Jamario Raman Moon''' (born June 13, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for one season at [[Meridian Community College]] and began his professional career with teams in the [[United States Basketball League]] and [[NBA Development League]], the [[Harlem Globetrotters]], and Mexican basketball team [[Fuerza Regia]] before signing with the [[Toronto Raptors]] in 2007. He has since played for the [[Miami Heat]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and [[Charlotte Bobcats]] of the NBA, along with the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the NBA D-League.

==Professional career==

===Early years===
After attending Coosa Central High School, Moon attended [[Meridian Community College]] where he played one season of [[college basketball]] for the Eagles in 1999–2000, averaging 20.8 points and 8.7 rebounds per game. After playing for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the 2001 NBA Summer League, Moon joined the [[Mobile Revelers]] for the 2001–02 season. He then joined the Dodge City Legend following the D-League season. After playing for the Los Angeles Lakers and the Utah Jazz in the 2002 NBA Summer League, he re-joined the Mobile Revelers for the 2002–03 season. He left the Revelers in November 2002.

Moon joined the Huntsville Flight via the 2003 D-League draft but was released by the team prior to the 2003–04 season. He re-joined them in January 2004, he was again released after just one game. After playing for the [[Harlem Globetrotters]] in 2004, he joined the [[Rockford Lightning]] for the 2004–05 season, but was released prior to the 2004–05 season. In December 2004, he joined the Kentucky Colonels before being released in February 2005.<ref name="Floyd County">{{cite web|last=LeMaster|first=Steve|title=Keathley-coached player Jamario Moon in the hunt for NBA championship|url=http://www.floydcountytimes.com/view/full_story/7181009/article-Keathley-coached-player-Jamario-Moon-in-the-hunt-for-NBA-championship|work=Floyd County Times|access-date=August 12, 2011|date=April 23, 2010|archive-date=September 27, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927030127/http://www.floydcountytimes.com/view/full_story/7181009/article-Keathley-coached-player-Jamario-Moon-in-the-hunt-for-NBA-championship|url-status=dead}}</ref> He then helped the Rome Gladiators win the 2005 World Basketball Association (WBA) championship. In December 2005, he joined the [[Albany Patroons]] before joining the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] in April 2006. He then played for [[Marietta Storm]] and [[Fuerza Regia]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.wbaball.net/newsarticle.php?article_id=7 |title=More WBA Signings |access-date=2014-11-11 |archive-date=2014-11-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141111181650/http://www.wbaball.net/newsarticle.php?article_id=7 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2006–07, he returned to the Albany Patroons. In 2007, he played for both the [[Gary Steelheads]] and Fuerza Regia.

===NBA===
Moon signed a two-year deal with the [[Toronto Raptors]] on July 10, 2007, after he had impressed the coaching staff in a three-day mini-camp held by the club.<ref name="colang">{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/features/moon_071128.html |author=Hareas, John |title=Raptors GM Bryan Colangelo on Jamario Moon |date=2007-11-28 |work=nba.com |access-date=2007-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026015447/http://www.nba.com/features/moon_071128.html |archive-date=2012-10-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=|first=|date=2007-07-10|title=Raptors Sign Jamario Moon|work=|publisher=[[Toronto Raptors]]|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/moonpr_071007.html|access-date=2007-11-11}}</ref> In his first start against the [[Chicago Bulls]], he had 12 [[point (basketball)|points]], six [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], three [[steal (basketball)|steals]], and one [[block (basketball)|block]] in 23 minutes. Moon remained in the starting lineup over the next few games, recording 15 points, nine rebounds, six blocks and three steals in another game against the Bulls on November 25. Two days later, Moon broke a club record by recording at least one block in twelve consecutive games.

On February 1, 2008, Moon was named NBA [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] Rookie of the Month. He had a career-high five steals on January 18 against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], and scored a career-high 17 points against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] the next night.<ref>{{cite news|author=Grange|first=Michael|date=2007-11-13|title=Overlooked rookie Moon making an impact|work=[[Globe and Mail]]|url=http://www.theglobeandmail.com/servlet/Page/document/v5/content/subscribe?user_URL=http://www.theglobeandmail.com%2Fservlet%2Fstory%2FLAC.20071113.RAPTORS13%2FTPStory%2FSports&ord=8053773&brand=theglobeandmail&force_login=true|access-date=2007-11-13}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/recap_112507.html |title=Calderon Leads Raptors Over Bulls |work=nba.com |access-date=2007-11-25}}</ref> Moon was invited to participate in two events at the 2008 [[NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[New Orleans, Louisiana]]. He scored 13 points for the rookies in the Rookie/Sophomore Challenge,<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20080215/RKESPH/boxscore.html NBA.com: 2008 Rookies at Sophomores BoxScore]</ref> and competed in the [[Slam Dunk Contest]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2008-01-21|title=Jamario Moon Selected for 2008 Sprite Slam Dunk|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/dunkcontest_moon_012108.html|access-date=2021-02-09|website=[[Toronto Raptors]]|language=en}}</ref> finishing behind winner [[Dwight Howard]] and 2007 defending champion [[Gerald Green]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/history/allstar/slamdunk_year_by_year.html#2008 |title=All-Star: Slam Dunk Year-by-Year Results 2008 RESULTS |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2009-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161219112512/http://www.nba.com/history/allstar/slamdunk_year_by_year.html#2008 |archive-date=2016-12-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On February 13, 2009, Moon was traded by Toronto to the Miami Heat, along with [[Jermaine O'Neal]] and conditional draft pick, for [[Shawn Marion]] and [[Marcus Banks]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2009-02-13|title=Raptors Acquire Marion And Banks From Miami|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/pressrelease_marion_021309.html|access-date=2021-02-09|website=[[Toronto Raptors]]|language=en}}</ref>
[[file:MoonHeat.jpg|Moon with the Heat in 2009|thumb|left|upright]]
On July 17, 2009, the Cavaliers signed Moon to an offer sheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=|first=|date=2009-07-20|title=Cavaliers Sign Jamario Moon to Offer Sheet|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/moon_090720.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090724094726/https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/moon_090720.html|archive-date=2009-07-24|access-date=2009-07-21|work=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref> On July 24, the Heat declined to match the offer, and Moon officially joined the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/moon_signed_090724.html | title=Cavaliers and Jamario Moon Enter Into Contract | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=2009-07-24 | access-date=2009-07-25}}</ref> The offer sheet is estimated to be worth $8.92 million over three years (the final year only being partially guaranteed).

On February 24, 2011, Moon was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] along with [[Maurice Williams (basketball)|Mo Williams]] in exchange for [[Baron Davis]] and an unprotected first round pick. The pick ended up #1 overall after the draft lottery, which the Cavaliers used to select [[Kyrie Irving]].<ref>{{Cite web| title = CLIPPERS ACQUIRE WILLIAMS AND MOON | url = http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews_110224.html | date = 2011-02-24 | access-date = 2011-02-24 | work =[[NBA.com]]}}</ref>

On March 2, 2012, Moon signed with the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120629164945/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/120302_moon.html|title=D-Fenders Acquire Jamario Moon}}</ref> That month, Moon was named Player of the Month in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/jamario_moon_player_of_month_2012_04_03.html|title=Los Angeles D-Fenders Jamario Moon Named NBA D-League Player of the Month|date=April 3, 2012|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=April 3, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406074041/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/jamario_moon_player_of_month_2012_04_03.html|archive-date=April 6, 2012}}</ref>

On April 15, 2012, Moon signed with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_moon_120415.html | title=Bobcats Sign Jamario Moon | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=2012-04-15 | access-date=2012-04-15 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120418215959/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_moon_120415.html | archive-date=2012-04-18 }}</ref> On July 2, 2012, he was waived by the Bobcats.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bobcats Waive Jamario Moon|url=http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2012/07/bobcats-waive-jamario-moon.html|work=HoopsRumours.com|date=July 2, 2012|access-date=July 2, 2013}}</ref>

Moon's final NBA game was played on April 26, 2012, in a 84–104 loss to the [[New York Knicks]] where he recorded 4 points, 2 assists and 8 rebounds.

===D-League and International career===
In November 2012, Moon was re-acquired by the Los Angeles D-Fenders. In November 2013, he was again re-acquired by the Los Angeles D-Fenders.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/1314_training_camp_roster.html 2013-14 Training Camp Roster] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610060051/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/1314_training_camp_roster.html |date=2016-06-10 }}</ref> In early January 2014, he left the D-Fenders.

On January 8, 2014, Moon signed with the reigning back-to-back [[Euroleague]] champions, [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]], for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=OLYMPIACOS PIRAEUS adds Moon|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/127704|date=January 14, 2014|access-date=January 8, 2014|work=Euroleague.net}}</ref> In March 2014, he was released by Olympiacos.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2014-03-02|title=Jamario Moon will part ways with Olympiacos?|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/112598/jamario-moon-will-part-ways-with-olympiacos.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140303190402/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/112598/jamario-moon-will-part-ways-with-olympiacos.html|archive-date=2014-03-03|access-date=2021-02-09|website=Sportando}}</ref> Later that month, he signed with [[Guaros de Lara (basketball)|Guaros de Lara]] for the 2014 [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto|LPB]] season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2014-03-28|title=Jamario Moon signs with Guaros de Lara|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/115078/jamario-moon-signs-with-guaros-de-lara.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328010950/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/115078/jamario-moon-signs-with-guaros-de-lara.html|archive-date=2014-03-28|access-date=2021-02-09|website=Sportando}}</ref>

On November 1, 2014, Moon was reacquired by the Los Angeles D-Fenders.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/141101_finalize_tc_roster.html D-Fenders Finalize Training Camp Roster] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106170005/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/141101_finalize_tc_roster.html |date=2014-11-06 }}</ref> On December 18, 2014, he was waived by the D-Fenders.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2014-12-18|title=D-Fenders Acquire Alfred Aboya|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/d-fenders-acquire-alfred-aboya/n-4906625|access-date=2021-02-09|website=OurSports Central|language=en}}</ref>

On January 5, 2015, Moon signed with Guaros de Lara for the 2015 [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto|LPB]] season, returning to the club for a second stint.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2015-01-06|title=Jamario Moon inks with Guaros de Lara|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/147494/jamario-moon-inks-with-guaros-de-lara.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150106012055/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/147494/jamario-moon-inks-with-guaros-de-lara.html|archive-date=2015-01-06|access-date=2021-02-09|website=Sportando}}</ref> On February 26, 2015, he was waived by the club.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2015-02-27|title=Jamario Moon waived by Guaros de Lara|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/153706/jamario-moon-waived-by-guaros-de-lara.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150227111814/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/153706/jamario-moon-waived-by-guaros-de-lara.html|archive-date=2015-02-27|access-date=2021-02-09|website=Sportando}}</ref>

In the summer of 2017, Moon played in [[The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]] for team Trained To Go.  He competed for the $2 million prize, and for team Trained To Go, he scored 13 points in 23 minutes on the court.  Moon and Trained To Go lost in the first round of the tournament to the Broad Street Brawlers 108–95.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bracket {{!}} The Basketball Tournament|url=https://www.thetournament.com/bracket|access-date=2018-02-22|website=www.thetournament.com|language=en|archive-date=2019-05-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514091135/https://www.thetournament.com/bracket|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On November 30, 2017, it was announced that Moon would be re-joining the [[Albany Patroons]] for his third stint with the team.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ward|first=Courtney|date=2017-11-30|title=Albany Patroons sign first three players|url=https://www.news10.com/news/albany-patroons-sign-first-three-players/|access-date=2021-02-09|website=[[WTEN]]|language=en-US}}</ref>

In December 2017, Moon briefly played in [[Uruguay]] with Club Atlético Aguada.<ref>[http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/america/uruguay/259632/former-nba-player-jamario-moon-aguada-part-ways.html Former NBA player Jamario Moon, Aguada part ways]</ref>

==Personal life==
In January 2009, Moon's wife, Tamara, gave birth to their first child.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Basketball/NBA/Toronto/2009/01/07/7945946-sun.html |title=Moon missing from lineup |first=Lance |last=Hornsby |work=Canoe.com |date=January 7, 2009 |accessdate=May 3, 2026 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307203054/http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Basketball/NBA/Toronto/2009/01/07/7945946-sun.html |archive-date=March 7, 2016}}</ref>

Jamario is the uncle of [[Xavier Moon]], who plays professional basketball for the [[Winnipeg Sea Bears]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].
